scope: Original documentation audit and destination plan. Coverage fields record the pre-implementation snapshot; current implementation and validation are documented in features-and-docs-validation.md.

coverage_definition.documented: Current reader docs give usable guidance for the feature; target may still require expansion.
coverage_definition.partial: Current MDX mentions all or part of the feature, but lacks usage steps, exact advertised breadth, or conditions. Comparison-only evidence is a claim, not a guide.
coverage_definition.missing: No relevant capability-specific coverage found in the inspected current MDX; generic category mentions do not count.

proposed_navigation.depth: For readers -> task group -> article; headings provide feature-level depth. No feature-per-page tree.

proposed_navigation.section_style: Use visual sidebar separators for task groups, not new nested category landing pages; keep flat file paths and no extra click to reach an article.

anchor_policy.syntax: Use explicit MDX heading IDs: ## Human-readable task title [#stable-anchor]. All mapped targets are proposed until content and headings exist.
anchor_policy.reason: Installed Fumadocs remarkHeading supports custom [#id] and otherwise generates GitHub-style slugs; explicit IDs prevent copy edits breaking homepage links.
anchor_policy.validation: Require every feature target page and fragment to exist in built output; validate exact 119-label equality, uniqueness, /docs/users/ prefix, nonempty anchor, and keyboard-accessible links.
anchor_policy.verification: Verified locally against installed Fumadocs implementation: running remarkHeading on synthetic MDX heading AST preserves explicit stable-feature-anchor, strips [#id] from heading text, emits matching TOC fragment, and generates reader-settings for an ordinary heading. This is plugin-level proof, not a built-page/browser check.
anchor_policy.existing_links: Retain existing sources, library, reading, install and getting-started paths. Preserve every current heading fragment on its original page, including library/#import-an-epub and reading/#mask-images, through retained headings or explicit legacy anchors with a useful summary and a link to the expanded guide. Do not redirect a whole page to replace a fragment: URL fragments are not sent to the server. Keep /docs/users/reading/#reader-settings, #read-offline, #listen-to-a-chapter and #when-a-chapter-does-not-load usable even when new guide pages take the detailed procedures.

navigation_changes: Keep /docs/users/ as the first-read landing page with two paths: install a source or import an EPUB.
Expand users/meta.json into task-group sections using existing source/library/reading/install URLs. List the 20 substantive articles above; do not list 119 feature headings in the sidebar.
Update docs index User guides and users index guide list for the new task-oriented tree.

Remove the homepage comparison CTA and comparison-led entry from primary reader navigation; keep /docs/comparison/ as an unpromoted legacy reference. Deleting or rewriting it is not required for this feature/docs implementation.
Existing comparison-only claims must not become procedural assertions until app behavior is verified.

Cross-link shared tasks: source EPUBs -> EPUB books; auto-download -> library updates + downloads; hidden categories -> privacy; history deletion -> history; app themes -> appearance, page themes -> reading.
assumptions_and_open_questions: Current feature labels are the source inventory, not independent runtime proof. The documentation audit itself did not inspect Android source; the later targeted source review is recorded separately in app-feature-evidence.md and does not verify all119 entries.
Proposed paths retain current readers URLs; new pages use flat user slugs grouped by sidebar task sections to avoid routing churn and excessive nesting.
21 reader pages including Getting started, of which 20 receive feature links, is the proposed depth tradeoff. Article grouping can be adjusted without changing exact source labels.

Exact menu labels, defaults, value ranges, supported engine options, permissions and persistence rules must be verified before drafting; caveats are research requirements where current MDX provides no answer.
Do not infer encryption, universal offline speech, cloud sync, entitlement bypass, unlimited cloud usage, or faithful rendering from broad feature names.
Keep /docs/comparison/ as an unpromoted legacy reference; do not use it as a feature destination. Rewriting or deleting its content is outside the required implementation scope.
Coverage classifications concern existing documentation, not app completeness. A partial item may already work fully in the app.
